content.user_title: Improve Code Quality With Clean Code Reviews
content.value_statement: Messy code slows reviews, refactoring, and feature work. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical Clean Code checks.
actual_capabilities: Applies naming guidance for variables, classes, and methods.
Reviews functions for size, single purpose, abstraction level, and argument count.
Assesses comments, formatting, object structure, error handling, tests, and class design.
Identifies code smells such as rigidity, fragility, immobility, and needless repetition.
Provides a checklist for clean code review and refactoring.
limitations: It provides guidance, not automated static analysis.
It does not execute tests or inspect runtime behavior.
It does not replace security review or performance profiling.
It may differ from a team's local style guide.

use_cases.title: Review Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Apply consistent Clean Code feedback before changes reach the main branch.

use_cases.title: Refactor Legacy Code
use_cases.description: Find unclear names, large functions, hidden side effects, and design smells before modifying old modules.

use_cases.title: Set Team Standards
use_cases.description: Turn Clean Code principles into shared review criteria for naming, comments, tests, and class design.

prompt_templates.title: Review Naming
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the selected code for intention-revealing names. Suggest clearer names for variables, functions, classes, and methods.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small change

prompt_templates.title: Check Function Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate each function for size, one clear purpose, abstraction level, side effects, and argument count. Prioritize the most useful fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Routine review of a feature branch

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this module with Clean Code principles. Identify code smells, rank refactoring steps, and explain the expected maintenance benefit.

prompt_templates.title: Create Review Criteria
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Clean Code review checklist for this repository. Cover naming, functions, comments, errors, tests, objects, and classes.

output_examples.input: Review a pull request with large functions and unclear names.
output: Highlights vague names that hide business intent.
Flags functions with mixed abstraction levels and too many responsibilities.
Suggests smaller reviewable changes with clearer tests.

output_examples.input: Refactor a legacy service before adding features.
output: Identifies side effects, long methods, and data structure leakage.
Ranks refactoring steps by clarity, risk, and maintenance value.
Recommends tests that protect behavior during cleanup.

output_examples.input: Create a shared Clean Code checklist for a team.
output: Groups review criteria by naming, functions, comments, errors, tests, and classes.
Keeps each checklist item actionable and easy to apply during review.

best_practices: Provide the relevant code and the team style guide together.
Ask for prioritized findings when reviewing large modules.
Pair refactoring advice with tests that protect existing behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for broad rewrites without a clear goal.
Do not treat every Clean Code guideline as an absolute rule.
Do not skip tests when changing behavior during refactoring.

faq.question: Does this skill modify code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance, refactoring suggestions, and checklists for a human or coding agent to apply.

faq.question: Can it help during pull request review?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure comments around naming, function size, comments, tests, and design smells.

faq.question: Does it replace a linter?
faq.answer: No. Linters catch mechanical issues, while this skill focuses on readability, intent, and maintainability.

faq.question: Can it review any programming language?
faq.answer: It uses language-neutral principles, but examples and final advice should respect the target language.

faq.question: Does it include security review?
faq.answer: Only indirectly. It improves clarity and error handling, but dedicated security review is still required.

faq.question: How should teams use it?
faq.answer: Use it as a shared review checklist, then adapt the guidance to repository conventions.
